response: Setting your AC to 24°C–26°C with a ceiling fan at low speed saves approximately 6% electricity per degree increase compared to running at 18°C–20°C. In Gujarat's climate, this reduces peak grid demand and lowers monthly bills significantly.
source: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) & GEDA Guidelines

response: In Gujarat (GERC tariff schedule), peak grid hours run from 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM (18:00–22:00 IST). Avoid running high-wattage appliances like washing machines, dishwashers, and water heaters during this window. Running them during daytime solar hours or late night saves cost and eases grid stress.
source: GERC Tariff Order & Gujarat DISCOM Regulations

response: Under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, residential consumers receive Central Financial Assistance (CFA) of ₹30,000 for 1 kW, ₹60,000 for 2 kW, and up to ₹78,000 for 3 kW and higher. Systems typically generate 4.3 kWh per kW per day in Gujarat, with a payback period of ~3.5 to 4 years.
source: MNRE Notification & PM Surya Ghar National Portal

response: Installing water-saving aerators on kitchen and bathroom taps can reduce water flow by 50% without dropping pressure. Fixing a slow drip saves up to 15,000 liters per year, and reduces municipal energy consumption needed to pump and treat water.

Carrying a reusable cloth tote bag and a stainless steel water bottle eliminates hundreds of single-use plastic items annually. Gujarat generates over 350 tonnes of plastic waste daily; source reduction is the most effective mitigation strategy.
source: Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) Annual Report

response: Segregate wet organic waste from dry recyclables at the source. Composting kitchen scraps at home or via municipal wet-waste collection prevents methane generation in landfills and creates rich organic compost for plants.
source: Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) & Mission LiFE Action Guide

response: Never dispose of electronic waste, batteries, or charger cables with municipal dry waste. Deposit them at authorized GEDA / CPCB collection centers to ensure toxic heavy metals like lead and cadmium are safely recovered and recycled.
